continuous_text.title: Where Are My Keys?
continuous_text.content:
Where are my keys, Mom?
Your keys are on the chair.
The chair? Which chair?
There are chairs everywhere!

There's a chair in the living room
And one in the bedroom, too.
There are chairs in the dining room.
I don't know which chair. Do you?

Your keys are where you left them.
Put on your glasses and see.
They're on the chair behind you.
My keys are there! Silly me!

continuous_text.title: A Family Visit
continuous_text.content:
Frame 1: Who are they, Jamie? They're my aunt and uncle. My aunt is my mom's sister.
Frame 2: These are my cousins. They're my aunt and uncle's children.
Frame 3: Where are your cousins now? They're in the kitchen. Look!
Frame 4: Where are they now? They're in my bedroom. They're jumping on my bed!
Frame 5: Jamie, where's the TV? It's in the living room.
Frame 6: Great! They're watching TV. They're quiet!

continuous_text.title: At the Museum
continuous_text.content:
1 Do you like to go to museums? I do! My favorite museum is the Science Museum. I love the old things there. There are some very old lamps at the museum. They're nearly 2,000 years old. They need oil in them. The oil burns.
2 There's an old computer at the museum, too. You can put a new computer on a desk or in a backpack, but this computer needs a big room.
3 This old TV at the museum is very funny. It's big, but the screen is small. I don't want it in my living room!
4 My favorite thing at the museum is an old bike. One of its wheels is very big and one wheel is very small. When you ride it, you sit on the big wheel. It's great!

Mom: Come on, girls! Where are your coats? Jack's wearing his.
Carla: We can't find ours.
Mom: Yours is there, Carla, under the table.
Carla: No, it isn't. That's Anna's coat. Hers is red. Mine is blue.
Mom: Oh, dear! Look! The dogs think your coat is theirs!

continuous_text.title: Household Objects
continuous_text.content:
1 In Sudan, some people keep their food cold in clay pots. They put one pot in another, with wet sand between them. A fridge needs electricity, but these pots don't. They can keep food cold anywhere.
2 Some people in Mali cook with a solar oven. A solar oven doesn't need fuel. It uses the sun. When this oven is in the sun, it's very hot, and it cooks the food quickly. This woman is cooking yam.
3 Do you like these chairs? This is a restaurant in Japan. The chairs don't have legs, but they're comfortable, and Japanese people like them.
4 Some people in Sarawak, Indonesia, sleep in hammocks. They don't use beds. The hammocks are clean and comfortable. When you don't need them, you can put them in a closet.

Look in my cookbook.
The food is good!
The food is cool!
